not unreadable files because there shouldn't be any to link
overlap_check: No existing methodology covers file acceptance. Related to 31 (no skip): this is what removes the 'unreadable' skip at the source. Related to 22/26 only by topic.

payload.name: Only What Can Be Read Is Linked
payload.description: A file is linked only if its type is accepted, and a type is accepted only if a reader can open it. Anything else is rejected at link time with the exact reason, so there is no unreadable state.

principles.name: Acceptance equals readability
principles.description: If a reader cannot open a file, it never links; a later 'unreadable' status is a sign that the gate at the door was wrong.

heuristics.condition: an 'unreadable' or 'not readable' status exists in code
heuristics.action: remove it; a read error after acceptance is a real failure to pause and retry

heuristics.condition: a fallback list of extensions per modality could re-admit a rejected type
heuristics.action: remove the fallback so one table decides

decision_rules.name: Link only what can be read
decision_rules.condition: a file is offered for linking
decision_rules.outcome: accept it only when its extension is in the one accepted table and the reader code can prepare it; otherwise reject at link time with the exact reason

decision_rules.name: Validate at link time
decision_rules.outcome: run the well-formedness check then; a malformed file is a link-time validation failure with its reason, not a later unreadable state

decision_rules.name: One table
decision_rules.condition: acceptance is decided in more than one place
decision_rules.outcome: keep a single source shared by the host and the link worker, and let no per-modality list admit a type the table rejects

decision_rules.name: Reader first
decision_rules.condition: a new modality or extension is proposed
decision_rules.outcome: add it to the table only together with the reader that opens it; a modality without self-describing files stays rejected with the exact reason, and is tracked as open rather than forgotten

decision_rules.name: Earlier links stay visible
decision_rules.condition: a file linked before this rule has an extension that is no longer accepted
decision_rules.outcome: show it as not accepted with the reason and the option to unlink; never delete it silently

decision_rules.name: A missing file resumes by itself
decision_rules.condition: a linked file no longer exists
decision_rules.outcome: record that it is missing and resume when the file watcher sees it again; do not treat it as unreadable
